title: Empirische Arbeit: From Knowledge Transfer to Learning by Expanding Together: Creating New Hybrid Forms of Activity through Research-Practice Partnerships
abstract: Across the globe, the influence of education research on policy and practice is limited by the fragility of connections among researchers, policy makers, and educators. Research-practice partnerships are a relational and systemic approach to promoting knowledge transfer that can support mutual learning across boundaries, though the approach differs from traditional, linear approaches to dissemination. This paper explores how one partnership’s activities supported a large school district’s process for adopting instructional materials in a way that integrated ideas and findings from research related to science teaching and learning. The paper explores how boundary crossing through boundary spanners, boundary practices, and artifacts supported the hybridization process. The analysis illustrates and helps theorize how successful knowledge transfer in research-practice partnerships entails transformation of activities through hybridization, rather than direct transfer of intact research-based practices into new settings.
